extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official final order describing disciplinary findings, legal conclusions, and sanctions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct for a registered patent practitioner. Covers jurisdiction, stipulated facts, the specific rule violation, mitigation, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) — failure to explain matters sufficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges she violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) (failing to explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies the specific factual basis: Respondent did not adequately inform the client that she believed the client had changed the scope of his invention such that additional fees would be required in advance to incorporate improvements into the nonprovisional application. Failure to communicate this resulted in the client's termination of the representation and request for fee refund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear communication of scope of representation and incorporation of client-supplied improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement letters/communications must make clear what work will be included (e.g., whether improvements submitted after a provisional filing will be incorporated into a later nonprovisional application) and under what terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/anti-pattern from the Order: the client believed improvements would be included at no additional charge; the practitioner and her agent believed additional fees were required. This lack of clarity led to a disciplinary violation. Best practice: explicitly state in engagement letters and follow-up communications whether post-provisional changes are included and any additional fees required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear disclosure of fee arrangements and allocation (including filing fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee arrangements in engagement letters must be clear (e.g., whether an advance payment is an hourly retainer to be billed against or is earmarked for filing fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the facts: the client believed $400 of a $5,200 payment was earmarked for filing fees; the respondent deposited the $5,200 into her IOLTA and later sought additional fees for new matter. Ambiguity about whether funds were for filing fees or an advance retainer contributed to the dispute. Ensure engagement letters specify what payments cover and how unused/earmarked amounts will be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling and return of client funds / refund of unearned fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are required to handle client funds appropriately (e.g., depositing into IOLTA where applicable) and to return funds that the client is entitled to (refund of filing fees/unearned legal fees) when requested or upon termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the client demanded return of all sums (including $400 he believed were filing fees); respondent did not respond, and the agreed sanction required a $400 refund within one month. The Order treats failure to refund as part of the misconduct context and remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and procedural authority for disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director (and OED) has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline under 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order frames the proceeding and settlement under these statutory/regulatory provisions, indicating the legal basis and procedures for OED enforcement and Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of settlement agreements to resolve disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary matters may be resolved by a Proposed Settlement Agreement submitted to and approved by the USPTO Director, which can set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Order is the product of a settlement agreement between the OED Director and the respondent. The Agreement resolves all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts and is approved as a Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigation and aggravation in imposing sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating and aggravating factors are considered in determining appropriate sanctions; the practitioner's prior disciplinary history (or lack thereof) is a mitigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes Respondent has no prior disciplinary history in fifteen years as a registered patent attorney; the OED Director considered this in mitigation when imposing sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible sanctions and remedial requirements for practitioner misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions imposed may include public reprimand, refund of client funds, mandatory continuing legal education (CLE) on law practice management, electronic publication of the Final Order, and publication of notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 27 lists agreed sanctions: (a) public reprimand; (b) refund $400 to the client; (c) attend a CLE seminar on law practice management within one year and provide proof; (d) OED to publish the Final Order in the electronic FOIA Reading Room; (e) OED to publish notice in the Official Gazette. These are examples of enforcement remedies and remedial education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of disciplinary records and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are publicly posted in the OED Reading Room and may be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires electronic publication at OED's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) and directs publication of the notice of public reprimand in the Official Gazette. Public disclosure may be part of disciplinary remediation and deterrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of appeal/review rights as part of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may waive rights to seek reconsideration, administrative review, or judicial appeal of a Final Order as part of a settlement agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, review under § 11.57, and otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of a disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in future matters involving the same or similar misconduct, in subsequent disciplinary proceedings, and in connection with reinstatement requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the record may be used (1) when addressing further complaints/evidence of same or similar misconduct, (2) as an aggravating factor in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent, and (3) in connection with any request for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
